marks.gloss_en: 'when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound heard' (II Chron 5:13) -- the Levites' song requires one unified voice
a priest is fit until he ages, i.e. until he trembles
a priest is fit for service from when he grows two pubic hairs
Rabbi's reason is Ezra 3:8, 'they appointed the Levites from twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the House of the Lord'
priests are called 'Levites' in twenty-four places in Scripture, so a verse about Levites can ground a law about priests
a minor is unfit for Temple service even if he is unblemished ('any man of your descendants')
the clause is Rabbi's view, and he holds there is no rabbinic disqualification at all between puberty and twenty
tokho-to-transmit / tokho-to-become-impure: just as the vessel transmits impurity through its airspace without contact, it becomes impure through its airspace without contact
what is pure in an earthenware vessel is impure in all other vessels, and what is pure in all other vessels is impure in an earthenware vessel
an earthenware vessel becomes impure from an impure item in its airspace
an earthenware vessel becomes impure from an item in its airspace even if the item never touched the vessel ('tokho', Lev 11:33)
the Torah testified that an impure earthenware vessel renders food in its airspace impure without contact -- even if it is full of mustard seeds
